newsitem.title: USA: Intertie rates cut by up to 414 MW this week.
newsitem.headline: Intertie rates cut by up to 414 MW this week.

text.p: Due to maintenance work, southbound transmissions on the DC (direct current) line of the Pacific Intertie will be cut by as much as 414 megawatts (MW) this week, while the AC (alternating current) line will be cut by 400 MW on Wednesday, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Tuesday.

BPA, which operates the Northwest portion of the interstate transmission system, said the AC line would be capped at 3,700 MW during hours ending 0900 through 1300 PT on Wednesday, compared with capacity of 4,100 MW.
Next Wednesday, May 28, the AC line was scheduled to be cut to 3,700 MW during hours ending 1500-1900 PT.
DC line usage was scheduled at 2,619 MW between hours ending 0900 through 1300 PT on Wednesday, compared with capacity of 2,990 MW.
For Thursday, southbound transmission on the DC line were scheduled at no more than 2,576 MW during hours ending 0800-1100 and 1400-1600 PT.
Transmissions were scheduled at the full 2,990 MW rate for Friday through next Tuesday, May 27.
On May 28, DC line usage is scheduled at 2,619 MW during hours ending 1500-1900 PT.
